![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/8de0dad0436135ef40aa26666d10659f4041275a915de153b6b4b45312c1c52f.png)

Evaluate ${∬}_{D}{x}^{2}y\,dA,$ where $D$ is the region shown in the picture above.
after.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into three type II regions ${D}_{1},$ ${D}_{2},$ and ${D}_{3},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/b58fc3909d5be467999053336f67d41b88b43c984208c60f3d46ee8b7479df58.png)

As a result, we get 

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,-2\le x\le -1},
$$

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1\le x\le 2}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{3}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,-2\le x\le 2}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{x}^{2}y\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}{x}^{2}y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}{x}^{2}y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{3}}{x}^{2}y\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{2}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{y\text{ }\,{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{-1}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{y\text{ }\,{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{3}{[\frac{y\text{ }\,{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7y}{3}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7y}{3}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{16y}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\cdot \frac{7}{3}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}+\frac{16}{3}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{7}{3}+\frac{64}{3} \\  & =\frac{71}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The region D can be partitioned into three type II regions D1, D2, and D3, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤y≤1,−2≤x≤−1},

D2={(x,y):0≤y≤1,1≤x≤2}

and

D3={(x,y):1≤y≤3,−2≤x≤2}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Dx2ydA=∬D1x2ydA+∬D2x2ydA+∬D3x2ydA=∫01∫−2−1x2ydxdy+∫01∫12x2ydxdy+∫13∫−22x2ydxdy=∫01[y x33]−2−1dy+∫01[y x33]12dy+∫13[y x33]−22dy=∫017y3dy+∫017y3dy+∫1316y3dy=2⋅73⋅[y22]01+163⋅[y22]13=73+643=713.

Question 2
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curves y=ex, y=ln⁡x, and the lines y=1+e−x and y=1−x, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫01∫1−yln⁡yf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
b
∫01/2∫1−y+eln⁡yf(x,y)dxdy+∫1/2e∫ln⁡y1−yf(x,y)dxdy
c
∫01∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫02∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫2e∫ln⁡ye−yf(x,y)dxdy
e
∫01∫−ye2yf(x,y)dxdy+∫12e∫−ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
Submit

decision.explanation: Horizontal slices change boundaries at y=1. For 0≤y≤1, the left boundary is x=1−y and the right boundary is x=e^y. For 1≤y≤e, the left boundary is x=ln(y) and the right boundary is x=1+e−y. These bounds give option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/4174f3930bb19223300539e1b4e9b7b191669aa4f701bff51e8349d0710ce6fb.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curves $y={e}^{x},$ $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ and the lines $y=1+e-x$  and $y=1-x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y={e}^{x} & \,⟹\,x=\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\ y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,x={e}^{y} \\ y=1+e-x & \,⟹\,x=1+e-y \\ y=1-x & \,⟹\,x=1-y\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/4df7cf2f33520a80270341d4a40b4a83d9f3c11ed8adb69fe1131a42bcd61d5a.png)

    

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1-y\le x\le {e}^{y}}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡y\le x\le 1+e-y}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-y}^{{e}^{y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}^{1+e-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curves y=ex, y=ln⁡x, and the lines y=1+e−x and y=1−x, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫01∫1−yln⁡yf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
b
∫01/2∫1−y+eln⁡yf(x,y)dxdy+∫1/2e∫ln⁡y1−yf(x,y)dxdy
c
∫01∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫02∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫2e∫ln⁡ye−yf(x,y)dxdy
e
∫01∫−ye2yf(x,y)dxdy+∫12e∫−ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows:

y=ex⟹x=ln⁡yy=ln⁡x⟹x=eyy=1+e−x⟹x=1+e−yy=1−x⟹x=1−y

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤y≤1,1−y≤x≤ey}

and

D2={(x,y):1≤y≤e,ln⁡y≤x≤1+e−y}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫01∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy.

content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/4174f3930bb19223300539e1b4e9b7b191669aa4f701bff51e8349d0710ce6fb.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curves $y={e}^{x},$ $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ and the lines $y=1+e-x$  and $y=1-x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y={e}^{x} & \,⟹\,x=\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\ y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,x={e}^{y} \\ y=1+e-x & \,⟹\,x=1+e-y \\ y=1-x & \,⟹\,x=1-y\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/4df7cf2f33520a80270341d4a40b4a83d9f3c11ed8adb69fe1131a42bcd61d5a.png)

    

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1-y\le x\le {e}^{y}}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡y\le x\le 1+e-y}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-y}^{{e}^{y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}^{1+e-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡y\le x\le 1+e-y}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-y}^{{e}^{y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}^{1+e-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤y≤1,1−y≤x≤ey}

and

D2={(x,y):1≤y≤e,ln⁡y≤x≤1+e−y}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫01∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy.

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curve y=x−2+1, and the lines y=2−12x and y=8−2x. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫01∫04−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
b
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
c
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−2yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫01∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
Submit

decision.explanation: The boundaries meet at (4,0), (2,1), and (3,2). For 0≤y≤1, horizontal slices run from x=4−2y to x=4−y/2. For 1≤y≤2, they run from the curve x=(y−1)²+2 to x=4−y/2. Therefore option b gives the required integral.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y=\sqrt{x-2}+1,$ and the lines $y=2-\frac{1}{2}x$ and $y=8-2x.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=\sqrt{x-2}+1 & \,⟹\,x=(y-1)^{2}+2 \\ y=2-\frac{1}{2}x & \,⟹\,x=4-2y \\ y=8-2x & \,⟹\,x=4-\frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/3f8e3ccfeac236d7fe9a502f599c61c404607a55ae809ec142019a3f881e1568.png)

  

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/3148cb0f499564db9cbfd6b635fef81dc47298789241af4a243c32dbf4dc8247.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,4-2y\le x\le 4-\frac{1}{2}y}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,(y-1)^{2}+2\le x\le 4-\frac{1}{2}y}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{4-2y}^{4-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{(y-1)^{2}+2}^{4-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curve y=x−2+1, and the lines y=2−12x and y=8−2x. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫01∫04−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
b
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
c
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−2yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫01∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows:

y=x−2+1⟹x=(y−1)2+2y=2−12x⟹x=4−2yy=8−2x⟹x=4−12y

Now, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤y≤1,4−2y≤x≤4−12y}

and

D2={(x,y):1≤y≤2,(y−1)2+2≤x≤4−12y}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option b: for 0≤y≤1, 4−2y≤x≤4−y/2; for 1≤y≤2, (y−1)²+2≤x≤4−y/2. The square-root curve requires y≥1, so its inverse cannot supply the boundary below y=1 as option d does.

content.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral Over a Union of Type II Regions
content.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y=\sqrt{x-2}+1,$ and the lines $y=2-\frac{1}{2}x$ and $y=8-2x.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=\sqrt{x-2}+1 & \,⟹\,x=(y-1)^{2}+2 \\ y=2-\frac{1}{2}x & \,⟹\,x=4-2y \\ y=8-2x & \,⟹\,x=4-\frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/3f8e3ccfeac236d7fe9a502f599c61c404607a55ae809ec142019a3f881e1568.png)

  

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/3148cb0f499564db9cbfd6b635fef81dc47298789241af4a243c32dbf4dc8247.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,4-2y\le x\le 4-\frac{1}{2}y}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,(y-1)^{2}+2\le x\le 4-\frac{1}{2}y}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{4-2y}^{4-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{(y-1)^{2}+2}^{4-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the line y=4−x2+2, and the lines y=−x and y=x, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a

b
∫−20∫−x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫4−x2+2−xf(x,y)dydx
c

d
∫−20∫x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫−x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx

decision.explanation: For −2≤x≤0, vertical slices extend from y=−x to y=√(4−x²)+2. For 0≤x≤2, they extend from y=x to the same upper curve. Splitting at x=0 gives option e.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/d185077fab32b6f2c85e53550da2f04f1128eb14610764ad131ed50d8bbc6ff0.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the line $y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2,$ and the lines $y=-x$ and $y=x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
after.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/47eccc29cbbdd917a247dec2f10329f718ed133b7e8398312b4ee3bc6bbbd647.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,-x\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,x\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-x}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the line y=4−x2+2, and the lines y=−x and y=x, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a
∫−20∫x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫4−x2+2−xf(x,y)dydx
b
∫−20∫−x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫4−x2+2−xf(x,y)dydx
c
∫−20∫−x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x−xf(x,y)dydx
d
∫−20∫x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫−x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx
e
∫−20∫−x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):−2≤x≤0,−x≤y≤4−x2+2}

and

D2={(x,y):0≤x≤2,x≤y≤4−x2+2}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−20∫−x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x4−x2+2f(x,y)dydx.

content.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral Over a Union of Type I Regions
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/d185077fab32b6f2c85e53550da2f04f1128eb14610764ad131ed50d8bbc6ff0.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the line $y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2,$ and the lines $y=-x$ and $y=x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
content.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/47eccc29cbbdd917a247dec2f10329f718ed133b7e8398312b4ee3bc6bbbd647.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,-x\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,x\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
